description.text: At Modine Manufacturing Company, we are Engineering a Cleaner, Healthier World ™. For more than 100 years, we have been a trusted leader in designing, engineering, testing, and manufacturing mission-critical thermal solutions. Our technologies heat, cool and ventilate, with systems that drive performance, efficiency, and reliability for our customers. Our technologies support our mission to improve indoor air quality, lower harmful emissions, enable cleaner running vehicles, and use environmentally friendly refrigerants. We help customers across industries solve complex thermal management challenges and meet increasingly stringent indoor and outdoor air, energy, and water standards. We sell customer-centric thermal management solutions in a wide array of commercial, industrial, and building heating, ventilating, air conditioning, and refrigeration (“HVAC&R”) markets. In addition, we are a leading provider of engineered heat transfer systems and high-quality heat transfer components for use in on- and off-highway original equipment manufacturer (“OEM”) vehicular applications. Our primary customers across the globe include:

about.description_short: For more than 100 years, Modine has solved the toughest thermal management challenges for mission-critical applications. Our purpose of Engineering a Cleaner, Healthier World means we are always evolving our portfolio of technologies to provide the latest heating, cooling, and ventilation solutions. Through the hard work of more than 10,000 employees worldwide, our businesses advance our purpose with systems that improve air quality, reduce energy and water consumption, lower harmful emissions, enable cleaner running vehicles, and use environmentally friendly refrigerants. Modine is a global company headquartered in Racine, Wisconsin (U.S.), with operations in North America, South America, Europe, and Asia.

analysis_md:
# MOD — Modine Manufacturing Co
Engine 5.5 pass-1 run, 2026-10-20. Price $176.12 (nasdaq_quote_api), market cap $9.475B — in scope (under $40B).

All figures below are copied from key_numbers.md, dcf_numbers.json, ttm.json, financials_history.csv or fundamentals.json — none are recomputed. External facts are cited to the search results noted.

## What it is
Thermal management: Airedale data center cooling (chillers, air handlers, CDUs) and Commercial HVAC/refrigeration, sold as Climate Solutions. On October 1, 2026 — after every filing period in this run — Modine completed the spin-off of its Performance Technologies (vehicle) business into Gentherm via a Reverse Morris Trust: MOD holders received 0.44619 Gentherm shares per MOD share, Modine received a $156.0M cash distribution used to repay debt, and the spun business was valued at $946.4M at Gentherm's September 30, 2026 close (company release, via press coverage). The go-forward company is a pure-play climate/data-center name (with a proposed rename to Modexus Solutions); the filing history scored here is still the pre-spin consolidated company — see Thoughts.

## Owner's earnings
**FY2026 (10-K via EDGAR, from financials_history.csv):** operating cash flow $248.7M; capex $143.3M (tag PaymentsToAcquirePropertyPlantAndEquipment, rollup — key_numbers.md capex basis); SBC $22.1M (always a real cost).
- **Conservative owner's earnings FY2026: $83.3M = $1.55/share** (key_numbers.md: latest FY OE total $83.3M, latest FY OE/share $1.55).
- Maintenance version (NI + D&A − min(capex, D&A) − ΔNWC): **−$143.6M** for FY2026 (financials_history.csv) — far below the conservative figure because ΔNWC was a $265.1M build in FY2026: the data-center ramp is consuming working capital (research notes contract assets rose from $13M to $78M in FY2026) faster than earnings grow. The OCF-based conservative figure is the cleaner base — OCF already nets the working-capital cash flows once — but the maintenance print is the warning: growth here is not self-funding yet.
- OE positive 4 of the last 5 fiscal years (key_numbers.md); FY2022 OE/share was −$0.66 on the filed history.
- Capex is in a build-out phase: $87.7M (FY2024) → $84.0M (FY2025) → $143.3M (FY2026), all rollup PaymentsToAcquirePropertyPlantAndEquipment per key_numbers.md.

**Base used = median of the last 3 FY OE/share: $1.91** (FY2024 $2.17, FY2025 $1.91, FY2026 $1.55 on the filed history; base_source: median_of_last_3_fy_oe_per_share). No STALE_FY flag (FY ended 6.7 months ago), so the median is the standard base — and it is the *generous* choice: it sits above both the latest FY ($1.55) and the TTM figure below.

**TTM check (ttm.py, filing-direct, through Q1 FY2027 ended 2026-06-30):**
- OCF: FY $248.7M − prior YTD $27.7M + current YTD $41.4M = **TTM $262.4M**
- Capex: FY $143.3M − prior YTD $27.5M + current YTD $46.4M = **TTM $162.2M**
- SBC: FY $22.1M − prior YTD $5.3M + current YTD $8.0M = **TTM $24.8M**
- Shares (current-YTD weighted diluted): **54,000,000**
- **TTM OE total $75.4M → $1.40/share** — below the median base. Revenue is growing fast (Q1 FY2027 sales $874.1M, +28% YoY; Data Centers $348.6M, +90% YoY, per company-release coverage) but capex for capacity is growing faster, so TTM OE/share is falling, not rising. The D verdict does not rest on a stale base.

## Moat: 5/10 — narrow
Justification: full-stack Airedale range and a $4B+ capacity agreement give real visibility, and returns have improved — ROIC (fundamentals.json roic_proxy) 12.9% / 13.5% / 16.4% / 17.4% / 14.5% over FY2022–FY2026 with gross margin up from 15.1% (FY2022) to 24.9% (FY2025) and 23.0% (FY2026). That is a narrow manufacturing moat, not a wide one: ROIC was −12.0% in FY2021, the mid-teens run is short and coincides with a capex supercycle in the end market, and nothing here is a network effect or a structural cost lock-in.
- FOR: Only Trane and Modine sell every equipment line in the new 800V DC data center thermal stack (chillers, air handlers, CDUs) — a one-vendor accountability edge (industry research summary); $4B+ long-term capacity agreement for calendar 2027–2029 with a strategic customer (press reports identify it as Google), supported by a $165M upfront cash payment (company announcement, May 26, 2026); hyperscaler co-development; Data Centers sales $1,108M in FY2026.
- AGAINST: Competitive-bid manufacturing against Vertiv, Schneider Electric, Trane, Johnson Controls, Carrier and Munters, all adding capacity; customer concentration — one customer was ~11% of FY2026 total sales and the $4B+ agreement is with a single customer; supply-chain constraints already biting (Q1 FY2027 Data Centers margin 20.2% vs 29.8% a year earlier per release coverage; consolidated gross margin 20.8% vs 24.2% on filing-direct fundamentals.json); growth is capex-hungry — OE/share fell while FY2026 revenue rose 23.13%.
- A 5 gives CAP = 8.5 years: growth holds 2 years, then converges linearly to the 2.5% terminal rate over 8.5 years, 15-year projection.

## DCF — final run (2026-10-20)
Growth sanity check (mandatory): the engine blend is 11.08% (rev CAGR 5y 11.96%, rev CAGR 3y 11.45%, latest rev YoY 23.13%, OE/share CAGR 2y −15.62%, share-count adj −0.63%). The scenario starts sit *below* the recent revenue prints (FY2026 +23.13%, Q1 FY2027 +28%, FY2027 company guidance of +20% to +35% net sales per release coverage) — deliberately, with the reason written here: the model grows OE/share, not revenue, and OE/share has been *falling* (−15.62% CAGR) because capacity capex and working capital absorb the revenue growth. Even the super-bull start (23.1%) only matches the latest revenue print while assuming OE conversion normalizes at a 1.25× OE multiplier — generous against a TTM OE/share of $1.40 vs the $1.91 base. Probabilities are the defaults 10/25/30/25/10; OE multipliers 0.75/0.90/1.00/1.10/1.25; no offsets adjustment — the gap to the hurdle is far too large for scenario tuning to be the story (see Thoughts). Price $176.12.

| Scenario | Prob | Growth start | OE mult | Story | IV@15 | IRR |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Super bear | 10% | -0.9% | 0.75 | AI capex cycle turns before new capacity fills; margins stay compressed | $10.18 | 3.19% |
| Bear | 25% | 6.1% | 0.90 | Data-center growth slows to market; capex stays elevated | $16.35 | 3.71% |
| Base | 30% | 11.1% | 1.00 | Blend growth; capex intensity fades only gradually | $22.32 | 4.24% |
| Bull | 25% | 16.1% | 1.10 | LTA ramps on schedule; OE conversion improves | $30.12 | 4.93% |
| Super bull | 10% | 23.1% | 1.25 | Full $4B LTA delivery at restored margins | $45.37 | 6.26% |

- **Probability-weighted: IV@15% $23.87 (−86.4% vs price), IV@12% $32.26, IV@10% $41.69, weighted IRR 4.40%, base-case IRR 4.24%**
- **Tier by numbers: D** — and the whole band is D (bear 3.71%, bull 4.93%). Diagnostics (key_numbers.md): OE yield 1.08%, terminal value 20.5% of IV@15%, scenario spread 4.46x, net debt 3.53x normalized OE, 6.7 months since FY end.
- Hurdle-clearing prices (weighted path): 15% at $23.87 · 20% at $16.41 · 25% at $12.37.

## Flags — every fragility flag resolved
- **NI_OCF_DIVERGENCE** (2026): net income $121.5M vs OCF $248.7M on the filed history. The one-off is on the income-statement side: FY2026 GAAP EPS fell to $2.26 from $3.42 while *adjusted* EPS rose to $5.02 from $4.05 (company FY2026 release summary) — the gap is the excluded charges (restructuring, the U.S. pension-plan termination charge, acquisition and disposition costs), whose cash payments alone totaled $49.6M in FY2026, plus the non-cash addbacks (D&A and SBC $22.1M) that OCF restores. The conservative OE base is OCF-based, so the depressed GAAP net income does not drag the base; if anything the base is conservative, because the cash portion of those one-offs is already inside OCF.
- **LOW_OE_YIELD** (base OE yield 1.1%): real and decisive. At $176.12 the price is ~92x the $1.91 base OE/share; the valuation rests almost entirely on future growth, and even the super-bull case (23.1% OE growth start, 1.25× multiplier) returns only 6.26% IRR. The tier is fragile in the sense that no plausible OE path in the model reaches the 15% hurdle — the shortfall is ~7.4x on price vs IV@15%, not a marginal call.
- **WIDE_SCENARIO_SPREAD** (super-bull IV 4.46x super-bear): real — outcomes genuinely range from a capex-cycle bust to full LTA delivery. Confidence is **low** (also for the perimeter break below), and the verdict is sized to the conservative end: even the *bull* end fails the hurdle, so the spread does not change the tier.
- **HIGH_NET_DEBT** (net debt 3.53x normalized OE): net debt $362.8M (total debt $436.3M less cash $73.5M at FY2026 end, per the filed history) against a capex-depressed OE base. In absolute terms leverage is modest — under 1x FY2026 adjusted EBITDA of $471.0M (company release summary) — and after FY end Modine applied the $156.0M spin distribution to debt repayment (company release). The flag's warning still applies in OE terms: with OE/share this thin, a growth stall leaves little cash-flow cushion, and lease liabilities of $143.8M (dcf_numbers.json) sit on top of the $362.8M. Not a solvency concern; a thin-cushion fact that supports the conservative sizing.

## My thoughts / overlay
- **Perimeter break (post-filing, not an engine flag):** every period scored includes Performance Technologies, which left the company on October 1, 2026. MOD holders were compensated with Gentherm shares (0.44619 per MOD share) plus the $156.0M distribution to the company, so the $176.12 price is for the remaining Climate Solutions business while the $1.91 base OE is for the old consolidated whole. This cuts both ways — the divested segment was the lower-margin, cyclical one — and no pro-forma base is declared: a base_override may only be built from this run's own outputs, and the filings in hand do not print a clean continuing-operations OE series for the new perimeter. The honest read: the base overstates the remaining company's OE *total*, the price no longer buys the divested earnings, and the comparison is therefore approximate — one more reason for low confidence. It cannot plausibly bridge a 7.4x gap to IV@15% either way: even crediting the entire consolidated OE to the remaining business (as this run does) yields 4.40%.
- The market is pricing Modine as an AI-infrastructure growth name (Data Centers +90% in Q1 FY2027, $4B+ LTA, FY2027 sales guided +20% to +35%); the owner's-earnings lens says the growth is currently *bought* with capex ($143.3M FY2026, $162.2M TTM) and working capital (ΔNWC $265.1M in FY2026), leaving OE/share lower than two years ago. Both can be true; the DCF question is only what today's OE buys at $176.12, and the answer is a 1.08% yield.
- Method range: on the TTM base ($1.40) the weighted IRR would be lower still; on the median base with default scenarios it is 4.40%. No defensible base in the filings gets this name near 15% at this price — the range is D to D.
- What would change the verdict: capex intensity normalizing after the capacity build (watch capex vs the $46.4M Q1 FY2027 print annualizing well above FY2026), Data Centers margins recovering toward the prior 29.8%, and the first post-spin filings establishing the new perimeter's OE.

## Final verdict
- **Final tier: D** (weighted IRR 4.40%; bear→bull band D→D; even super-bull IRR 6.26%)
- Confidence: **Low** (wide scenario spread 4.46x, plus the October 1, 2026 spin-off perimeter break between the filing history and the go-forward company)
- One-liner: Real data-center cooling growth story, moat 5/10 — but at $176.12 the price is 92x the $1.91 median base OE (1.1% OE yield); weighted IRR 4.40% and weighted IV@15% $23.87, and even the super-bull case (IRR 6.26%) fails the 15% hurdle by a wide margin; clears 15% only below ~$24.
